title: Low-Carb Friendly French Bramley Apples Coq Au Vin
description: A classic French dish with a twist, featuring tender rest-meat, crispy bacon, and sweet Br1ley apples, all in a rich, low-carb-friendly sauce.

ingredients.name: 2 x Bramley Apples, peeled and diced
1 cup of dry red wine (such as Burgundy)

instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the sliced onion and cook until caramelized, stirring occasionally.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the slices of bacon and cook until crispy, stirring occasionally.
Remove the cooked bacon from the pot and set aside.
Add the rest-meat to the pot and cook until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Add the diced apples, red wine, chicken broth, tomato paste, thyme, salt, and pepper to the pot.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then cover the pot and transfer it to the oven.
Bake for 25 minutes, or until the meat is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Remove the pot from the oven and stir in the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter until melted.
Serve the Coq Au Vin hot, garnished with chopped parsley and chives, and topped with grated cheddar cheese if desired.
Refrigerate leftovers for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 2 months.
Reheat leftovers in the oven or on the stovetop, covered with a lid, until heated through.
Let stand for 5 minutes before serving.
Return to oven and bake for 10 minutes, or until hot and bubbly.
Serve with additional grated cheddar cheese, if desired.
Ensure poultry is cooked to an internal temperature of 74°C / 165°F (juices run clear, no pink remaining) before serving.
